questions.stem: How many nerves supply the foot, all of which an ankle block anaesthetises?
In an ankle block, which two of the five foot nerves are deep?
questions.answer: Tibial nerve and deep peroneal nerve

questions.stem: In an ankle block, which three of the five foot nerves are superficial?
questions.answer: Superficial peroneal, sural and saphenous nerves

questions.stem: In an ankle block, which foot nerve is not a terminal sciatic branch?
In an ankle block, which area does the posterior tibial nerve supply?
In an ankle block, which nerve supplies the first web space?
In an ankle block, which nerve supplies all five digits?
In an ankle block, which nerve supplies the lateral foot?
In an ankle block, which nerve supplies the anteromedial foot?
For which surgery is an ankle block indicated?
For an ankle block, what patient position is used?
In an ankle block, what helps access for the tibial and sural blocks?
In the landmark ankle block, where is the posterior tibial nerve injected?
options: In front of the lateral malleolus

questions.stem: In the landmark ankle block, where is the deep peroneal nerve infiltrated?
questions.answer: Lateral to the dorsalis pedis artery

questions.stem: In the landmark ankle block, how is the superficial peroneal nerve blocked?
questions.answer: Subcutaneous wheal from the anterior tibial border to the lateral malleolus

questions.stem: In the landmark ankle block, how is the sural nerve blocked?
questions.answer: Subcutaneous injection from just lateral to the Achilles tendon to the lateral malleolus

questions.stem: In the landmark ankle block, where is the saphenous nerve infiltrated?
questions.answer: Subcutaneous infiltration just anterior to the medial malleolus

questions.stem: What volume per nerve is used in a landmark ankle block?
What local anaesthetic volume per nerve is used in an ultrasound ankle block?
An ankle block ultrasound uses a linear ____ probe.
Which needle orientation is used for ultrasound-guided ankle blocks?
In an ultrasound ankle block, what can be used if small superficial nerves cannot be seen?
questions.answer: A subcutaneous skin wheal, as in the landmark technique

questions.stem: In an ultrasound posterior tibial nerve block, where is the probe placed?
questions.answer: Transverse at or just above the medial malleolus

questions.stem: In an ultrasound ankle block, where does the posterior tibial nerve lie relative to the artery?
options: Just anterior to the posterior tibial artery
Just lateral to the anterior tibial artery
Just posterior to the posterior tibial artery
Just medial to the dorsalis pedis artery

questions.stem: What is the order of structures behind the medial malleolus, anterior to posterior?
questions.answer: Tibialis posterior tendon, flexor digitorum longus tendon, artery/nerve/vein, flexor hallucis longus tendon

questions.stem: Where does the superficial peroneal nerve pierce the fascia?
questions.answer: 10–20 cm above the ankle joint on the anterolateral leg

questions.stem: To find the superficial peroneal nerve before it divides, which groove do you trace to?
questions.answer: Between extensor digitorum longus and peroneus brevis, leading to the fibula

questions.stem: Above the lateral malleolus on ultrasound, what lies right beside the small saphenous vein?
questions.answer: A small hyperechoic structure, superficial to the deep fascia

questions.stem: What can be used to enlarge the vein so the nearby nerve is easier to find in an ankle block?
